transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s been going on a long time. Almost two years, I guess. I’m here because I know the contractor and some people on my block have been working together, quietly, to cheat us. They keep leaving my kitchen wrong on purpose, and everyone keeps making excuses, even when my husband shows receipts. I’m tired of being treated like I don’t see what’s happening.
Can you tell me more about what makes you believe the contractor and people on your block are working together to cheat you?

It’s just… it keeps happening the same way. For nearly two years, the kitchen is still not right, and every time we point it out, there’s some excuse. My husband has shown receipts and all that, but it doesn’t change anything. I know the contractor isn’t doing this alone. Some people on the block are in on it too, quietly, to make us pay and keep things half-wrong.
Do you believe these people are working against you even though you don’t have clear proof of their collusion?

Yes… I do. I know I don’t have, you know, papers saying they’re all together, but I’m sure of it. For almost two years this kitchen has stayed half-wrong, and every time my husband shows receipts, they just give excuses. It feels deliberate.
Have you ever felt that people are plotting against you in other situations, outside of the issues with the contractor and your neighbors?

Not really outside of this… I mean, this is the thing. The contractor, and some people on the block—I've been sure they're working together to cheat us, keeping the kitchen wrong on purpose. My husband shows the receipts, and they still just make excuses. So… mostly that.

latest_inference.note: The patient's belief is focused on a specific group (contractor and neighbors) related to a prolonged situation without evidence of broader delusional themes or other psychotic symptoms. This aligns more with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22.0) or Persistent Delusional Disorder (F23.2). Other psychotic disorders have been ruled out due to absence of hallucinations, disorganization, or mood symptoms.
